name: Gujarat Fluorochemicals Ltd
_note: Fact base for the initiation as of 30-Sep-2026. Every item carries src (URL) and published (date). Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026 are used.

shp.title: Shareholding pattern, quarter to Jun-2026 (BSE data via Trendlyne)

businessLines.name: Fluoropolymers
businessLines.products: PTFE, micro-powders, PFA, PVDF, FEP, FKM (fluoroelastomers), PPA
businessLines.uses: Chemical processing, oil & gas, semiconductors, wire & cable, automotive, EV batteries (PVDF), solar, hydrogen, data centres
businessLines.note: India's largest fluoropolymer producer; plants at Dahej (2007) and Jolva; exports to Europe, the US and Asia through GFL GmbH and GFL Americas

businessLines.name: Fluorochemicals
businessLines.products: Refrigerants R22, R32 (from Mar-2026; retrofit volumes from Q1FY26), R125, R410a, R407c; R134a under construction; HF-, TFE- and KF-based fluorospecialties for agro and pharma
businessLines.note: Largest R22 producer in India; Ranjitnagar refrigerant plant (1989); R32 10kt, doubling to 20kt

businessLines.name: Bulk chemicals
businessLines.products: Caustic soda, chloroform, methylene dichloride, carbon tetrachloride
businessLines.note: Feedstock integration: chloroform feeds R22, which feeds TFE and PTFE

businessLines.name: Battery materials (GFCL EV Products Ltd)
businessLines.products: LiPF6 salt, electrolyte formulations, additives, LFP cathode active material, PVDF/PTFE binders; natural-graphite anode under construction
businessLines.note: Integrated battery complex at Jolva (Dahej); portfolio covers ~70% of the cost of an LFP cell; GFL owned 96.89% at Mar-2026

call.fact: Growth from higher-value grades and new fluoropolymer volumes; 'marginal' input-cost price increases; new fluoropolymer capacity nearly fully utilised; 15-20% growth 'absolutely visible' for this year and next; most customer approvals by end-FY27 with volumes rising in H2.
3M's exit fully absorbed over two years; AGC's proposed UK plant closure is bringing customer enquiries and qualifications, traction 'a quarter or 2 down the line'.

10,000 t R32 plant fully utilised; expansion to 20,000 t to be commissioned in Q2FY27 with full utilisation expected in CY27; 40-50% of R32 sold on long-term contracts; export and domestic prices 'very close'. R134a (brownfield, TCE imported) by end-FY27; AHF capacity added in phases from Q3FY27.
Quota expected to follow the formula (baseline plus 2024-26 production); GFL is adding capacity to use its full entitlement across R32, R134a, R22 and R125.

LiPF6 has almost finished qualification and is in its growth phase; PVDF close to qualification; LFP cathode revenue towards end-FY27; 'significant traction' towards end-FY27 and FY28; three-digit quarterly revenue targeted in Q4FY27; full potential from FY28 onwards given ~1.5 years of stabilisation and qualification.

The ~US$216 mn Oman battery-materials project is on hold for geopolitical reasons and moved to Dahej; the ~Rs 1,200 cr sovereign (OIA) funding approved for Oman will not be available for India; 'our fundraise process is on'.
FY27 capex Rs 2,300 cr in EV and ~Rs 800 cr in chemicals; cumulative EV plan Rs 6,000 cr; CWIP Rs 1,900 cr at Mar-2026.
Gap between standalone and consolidated widened because some CIF consignments booked earlier in the German and US trading subsidiaries were reversed in the standalone accounts.

guidance.value: Rs 6,000 cr cumulative capex by FY28; ~2x asset turns; EBITDA margin above 25%; full earnings potential of current investments by FY29

guidance.item: Revenue potential of EV investment already made (~Rs 2,000 cr)
guidance.value: ~Rs 3,000 cr, after 9-12 months of qualification per plant
Rs 500-700 cr with EBITDA break-even (IDBI Capital, 22-Jul-2026; not repeated on the Q1 call)
Rs 3,150 cr: Rs 2,300 cr EV; Rs 850 cr chemicals (Rs 250 cr fluoropolymers, Rs 222 cr electronic chemicals, Rs 150 cr refrigerants)

capitalStructure.ccps: GFCL EV issued Rs 430 cr of Series A CCPS to the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in FY26; convertible into GFCL EV equity under a formula in the shareholders' agreement (not disclosed); carried at fair value as a liability; Rs 340 cr unspent at Mar-2026
capitalStructure.warrants: GFCL EV allotted 5.71 cr warrants at Rs 35 to the promoter group on 12-Nov-2024 (Rs 200 cr; Rs 50 cr paid); balance Rs 150 cr paid and shares issued on 8-May-2026. Related-party note: Vivek Jain, Devansh Jain and Nandita Jain
capitalStructure.privatePlacement: GFCL EV issued 2.64 cr shares at Rs 35 (Rs 92.5 cr) in FY26; GFL's stake 96.89%

history.event: Gujarat Fluorochemicals set up by the Inox group (Jain family); refrigerant plant at Ranjitnagar commissioned in 1989
Dahej complex commissioned: PTFE, the start of the fluoropolymer business

NCLT approves the demerger of the chemicals business of the old GFL (now GFL Ltd) into Inox Fluorochemicals, renamed Gujarat Fluorochemicals; appointed date 1-Apr-2019; listed in Oct-2019 (third-party source)
Refrigerant and PTFE upcycle: revenue Rs 5,685 cr and net profit Rs 1,323 cr in FY23 (EBITDA margin 35%)
Downcycle: revenue -25%, net profit -67% as Chinese fluoropolymer and refrigerant prices fell and customers destocked
Promoter group subscribes to Rs 200 cr of GFCL EV warrants at Rs 35
IFC invests Rs 430 cr in GFCL EV (CCPS); R32 production and sales start (Mar-2026); FY26 revenue Rs 4,996 cr, net profit Rs 574 cr
Founder and chairman Devendra Kumar Jain dies; Vivek Jain becomes chairman and MD (Feb-2026)
GFL files a fresh anti-dumping case on Chinese and Russian PTFE (the Sep-2025 recommendation was apparently not imposed)
Q4FY26: EV losses widen (EBITDA -Rs 45 cr); consolidated PAT Rs 112 cr (-32%); stock falls; warrant shares issued in GFCL EV
R134a capacity announced (29-Jun); GFCL Semiconductor and Advanced Materials Ltd incorporated; exchanges' no-objection (9-Jul) to the scheme merging promoter company Inox Leasing and Finance into GFL
Q1FY27: revenue +24%, EBITDA +24%, PAT +20%; fluorochemicals +52% on R32; Oman project put on hold

management.name: Vivek Jain
management.note: Promoter; chairman from 12-Feb-2026 after the founder's death

management.name: Dr. Bir Kapoor
management.note: Re-appointment proposed at the 2026 AGM; also granted ESOPs in GFCL EV (FY26 charge Rs 8.21 cr)

management.name: Sanath Kumar Muppirala, Sunil Kumar Singh Chauhan, Niraj Kishore Agnihotri, Jignesh Parmar

governance.auditor: Patankar & Associates (Pune); unqualified opinion on FY26 accounts
governance.pledgeJun26: 5.97% of promoter shares (40.26 lakh shares; ~3.7% of the company): Devansh Trademart LLP 74% of its holding, Aryavardhan Trading LLP 19%
governance.promoterSellingFY26: Devansh Trademart LLP's stake fell from 4.84% to 3.65% in FY26
governance.scheme: Composite scheme: Inox Leasing and Finance (holding company) demerges its wind business into Inox Holdings and Investments and then merges into GFL, so the family would hold GFL shares directly; exchanges' no-objection 9-Jul-2026; further approvals pending
relatedParties: Guarantees and securities for group companies' loans: Rs 498 cr at Mar-2026 (Rs 422 cr at Mar-2025); Rs 1,521 cr of exposure released in FY25 (mainly Inox Wind)
Investment of Rs 177 cr in optionally convertible preference shares of group renewable-power companies (IGREL Mahidad Rs 153 cr, Flurry Wind Rs 24 cr) that supply captive power; power bought Rs 49 cr
Promoter family holds warrants/shares in GFCL EV bought at Rs 35 (Rs 200 cr)
ESOPs in GFCL EV to KMP: 75 lakh options at Rs 1 exercise price (FY26 grant), against share issues at Rs 35

accounting.fact: Net foreign-exchange gain Rs 88.6 cr in FY26 (Rs 57.8 cr in FY25) is in other income in the annual accounts but inside the company's segment EBITDA (Rs 1,290.7 cr vs Screener's Rs 1,201 cr).
Company ROCE (14.05% FY26) and ROE (12.17%) exclude capital employed in capacity expansions of the last two years and CWIP; reported ROE on total equity was ~7.6%.
Classified as a financial liability at fair value through profit or loss; fair-value changes will hit the P&L.
Rs 19.5 cr labour-code charge in FY26 (Q3, Q4).
Q4FY25 PAT included a Rs 29 cr deferred-tax gain; battery losses get little tax credit (group tax rate 29% in FY26).
Inventory 453 days and receivables 94 days of revenue in FY26 (Screener); the company counts 192 working-capital days at Mar-2026 and 149 at Jun-2026.
